JB One is an operations app for gold and silver jewellery retailers, used by shop staff to print jewellery tags and prepare customer estimates. It also has a web catalogue that each shop can publish, described in section 10. This policy explains what information JB One handles, why, and the choices available to you. JB One is built for internal use inside a jewellery shop, installed and set up by the shop's owner for their own staff, rather than distributed as a general consumer app.

01Information we collect

  • Staff account details. A username and password for each staff member, set up by the shop's administrator to control who can access which part of the app. Accounts are configured by the shop, not self-registered by staff.
  • Business data entered by staff. Jewellery item details (metal purity, description, weight, the Hallmark Unique ID) used to print tags, and customer estimate figures (weight, rate, charges) used to print or share a receipt. This is operational business data, not personal data about staff beyond their login username.
  • Photos staff choose to upload. If staff use Shop Login to add a product photo, the photo they pick or take is sent to the shop's own catalogue website.
  • Shop configuration. Metal purity lists, tax rules, and printer/label settings chosen by the shop owner, stored in a configuration file the owner controls in their own Google Drive.

We do not collect precise or coarse location, contacts, microphone audio, call logs, or SMS content, and the app does not read your camera or photos in the background.

02How permissions are used

PermissionWhy the app asks for it
BluetoothTo find and print to the shop's thermal label or receipt printer over Bluetooth.
LocationRequired by Android itself before any app can scan for nearby Bluetooth devices, on phone software older than Android 12. JB One does not read, store, or transmit your location.
Storage / filesTo import a spreadsheet of items for bulk tag printing, to choose a logo image for a label, and to save exported PDFs on older Android versions.
InternetTo fetch the day's gold/silver market rate, sync the shop's shared configuration, and, for the administrator only, sign in to Google Drive.

The app does not ask for the camera or microphone permission. If staff choose to take a photo for a product in Shop Login, Android opens its own camera or photo picker for that one photo.

03How we use information

Solely to operate the features described above: printing tags and receipts, calculating estimates, keeping shop-wide settings in sync across devices, and showing the day's metal rate. We do not use any information for advertising, and we do not build profiles of individual users.

04Third-party services

  • Google Sign-In & Google Drive are used only by the shop's administrator, to store and retrieve the shop's shared configuration file. Google's handling of that data is governed by Google's own Privacy Policy.
  • Google Play provides in-app updates and the in-app review prompt. Google's handling of that is governed by Google's own Privacy Policy.
  • The shop's own catalogue website is opened inside the app for Shop Login and Public Page. What you do on that website is handled by the shop that runs it (see section 10).
  • A public gold/silver rate page is read to show the day's market rate; no personal information is included in that request.

We do not use advertising networks or analytics/tracking SDKs of any kind, and we do not sell or rent information to third parties.

05Data storage & retention

Business data entered on a device (item lists, estimates, saved label designs) is stored locally on that device and used to drive printing. Your login session is stored locally on the device and is removed automatically when the app is uninstalled. The shared shop configuration lives in the administrator's own Google Drive for as long as the shop chooses to keep it there.

06Data sharing

We do not share information with third parties for their own marketing or advertising purposes. Information leaves a device only when a staff member deliberately connects to a printer and sends a print job, deliberately shares a receipt (for example, over WhatsApp or as a PDF), when staff upload a product photo to the shop's catalogue website, or when the administrator saves shop configuration to their own Google Drive.

07Children's privacy

JB One is a business tool for retail staff and is not directed at, marketed to, or knowingly used by children. We do not knowingly collect information from anyone under 13 (or the relevant minimum age where you live).

08Your choices

Because JB One is deployed by a shop for its own staff, requests about a staff account (adding, changing, or removing one) are usually handled directly by that shop's administrator. To ask about data related to your own use of the app, or to request that information be corrected or deleted, contact us using the details below.

09Security

We use encrypted network connections and a signed application package to protect information handled by the app. No method of storage or transmission is completely secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.

10JB One Web (the online catalogue)

Each shop can publish an online catalogue on its own web address, with an admin back office for the shop's staff. This section covers that web catalogue.

  • Visitors. Browsing needs no account. A wishlist and enquiry list, where the shop has switched them on, are saved in the visitor's own browser on their device. The shop's dashboard counts how often each product is viewed or added to a wishlist, without identifying the visitor.
  • Enquiries. An enquiry opens a WhatsApp message in the visitor's own WhatsApp, addressed to the shop's number. The message is between the visitor and the shop.
  • Customer accounts. Only if a shop switches on online purchase, a customer can register with a name, mobile number, password and delivery address, and place orders. That information is visible to that shop.
  • Shop staff. Staff sign in with a mobile number and password set by the shop owner. Product details and photos they add are stored on the server that hosts the catalogue.
  • Fonts and rates. The catalogue pages load typefaces from Google Fonts and read a public gold and silver rate page. No personal information is included in those requests.

11Changes to this policy

We may update this policy as the app changes. Material changes will be reflected by updating the effective date at the top of this page.
